senses.d: To make suitable; to make to correspond; to fit or suit.
To fit by alteration; to modify or remodel for a different purpose; to adjust.
ex: to adapt a story for the stage
to adapt an old machine to a new manufacture

senses.d: To make by altering or fitting something else; to produce by change of form or character.
ex: to bring out a play adapted from the French
a word of an adapted form

senses.d: To make oneself comfortable to a new thing.
ex: They could not adapt to the new climate and so perished.

senses.d: Adapted; fit; suited; suitable; apt.
ex: This prediction, though somewhat obscure, is wonderfully adapt.

senses.d: One who is capable of adapting to differing situations.
ex: He was an able adapter, and could easily adjust to the differences when the company changed ownership.

senses.d: One who adapts a thing, e.g. a play.
ex: The critic gave rave reviews to the adapter of the ancient play, who worked to give the text more relevance to the modern day.

senses.d: A device or application used to achieve operative compatibility between devices that otherwise are incompatible.
ex: He had an adapter that let him plug his phone into the car's cigarette lighter for power.

senses.d: Specifically, a device that permits two or more plugs to be used at a single electrical power point.
ex: The wall outlet sprouted an electrical monstrosity of adapters plugged into adapters that sparked ominously.

senses.d: Specifically, a device that allows one format of plug to be used with a different format of socket.
ex: We bought adapters to use our three-prong plugs in the two-prong, unpolarized outlets of the old house.

senses.d: Specifically, an AC adapter: a device that reduces voltage and converts AC to DC to allow a battery-powered device to use mains power.
ex: I lost my cellphone's adapter so I couldn't recharge it.

senses.d: A collection of low-rank matrices which, when added to a base model, produces a fine-tuned model; a LoRA.

grp.label: device allowing more plugs at an outlet
device allowing plug to fit in an outlet of different type

ety.text: Inherited from Old Spanish ladron, from Latin latrōnem. Cognate with Ladino ladrón.

pt:T.gl: adaptor (device allowing more plugs at a socket)

ety.text: The second sense is probably from Benjamin Electric Manufacturing Company, an American company that made early electrical accessories like adaptors.

senses.d: The process of adapting something or becoming adapted to a situation; adjustment, modification.
A change that is made or undergone to suit a condition or environment.
ex: It's staggering because these adaptations to your schedule can dramatically change your life forever.

senses.d: The process of replacing a given morpheme of a source lexeme with an equivalent morpheme of the target lexeme, especially where the two morphemes are cognates.
The process of change that an organism undergoes to be better suited to its environment.
An instance of an organism undergoing change, or the structure or behavior that is changed.
The process of adapting an artistic work from a different medium.
ex: Plays are rich and suitable sources for adaptation to film.

senses.d: An artistic work that has been adapted from a different medium.
The means by which social groups adapt to different social and physical environments.
